To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel method for screening and characterizing the products of the deacetylation reaction of chitosan by an enzyme, acetyl xylan-esterase A, and that this enzyme is able to deacylate a range of chitooligosacharide products, but not to fully deacetylase chitooligoscharides to chitooligoschacrides.

1) we developed an HILIC-UV method for chitooligosacharides analysis, 2) the method was used to analyze the products of the deacetylation reactions catalyzed by the native AxeA and two of its mutants, and 3) the mutants produced a greater variety of products than the native AxeA.
we have developed an HILIC-UV method that can be used to determine the deacetylation profile of chitooligosacharides produced by acetyl xylan-esterase A (Axe A).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a directed evolution approach for obtaining chitooligosacharide variants that can be used in pharmaceutical, cosmetic and nutraceutical applications.
the discovery of enzymes with new and improved activities and the development of new analytical methods for their characterization.
the development of a new enzyme-based method to produce chitooligosaccarides with defined structures and properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HILIC-UV/MS/MS methodology developed here is an effective tool for the analysis of deacetylated products of chitinous oligomers and that directed evolution of the acetyl xylan enzyme is a promising approach to obtain enzymes that are able to produce chitooligosacharides with well-defined properties.
the deacetylation activity of the AxeA variants is not sufficient to generate a product with a high enough concentration of (GlcN)n oligomers to be industrially useful.
the AxeA variants produced by directed evolution have a higher activity toward chitosan oligomers and that the HILIC-UV method is a suitable method for profiling deacetylation reactions of oligomers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HILIC-ESI-MS/MS method is suitable for profiling the products of the deacetylation reaction of (GlcNAc)(6) and the random mutagenesis strategy can be used for directed evolution of enzymes for chitosan oligomer production.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of a HILIC method to profile chitooligosacharides and have shown the potential of the HILIC-ESI-MS/MS technique to provide detailed structural information on the deacetylation activity of AxeA variants.
we were able to develop a method to profile deacetylated oligosaccharide products of chitin deacetylase variants and that the method can be used as a tool to screen for chitin deacetylation variants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HILIC mode of LC coupled with mass spectrometry provides a rapid and sensitive method for characterizing the deacetylation activity of enzymes on chitooligomers.
HILIC is a useful technique for characterizing the deacetylation product mixtures of chitooligosacharides.
the deacetylation activity of AxeA is highly substrate specific and that the deacetylases from different organisms may have different specificities.
